paragraphs.source_en: European civilization is ahead of ours, and so this system has been practiced there much earlier than in Japan. Even when parents and children happen to live together, a son pays interest on money borrowed from his father, or pays board like any stranger. Only because parents acknowledge the son’s individuality and pay it respect can such a fine custom be established. Sooner or later, this fashion must certainly be imported into Japan as well. Relatives have already grown distant, and parents and children are now separating. The development of individuality, only barely held in check, and the respect that grows along with that development will increase without limit, so unless people separate still further, life will feel cramped. But now that fathers, sons, and brothers have already separated, there is no one left to separate from; therefore, as the final measure, husbands and wives naturally separate. People nowadays suppose that living together is what makes a husband and wife; that is an egregious misconception. In order to live together, their individualities must be compatible enough for them to live together. In the old days there was no problem at all: people spoke of two bodies with one heart, and though the eye saw a husband and wife, in reality they amounted to only one person. That is why they talked of growing old together and sharing the same grave, even turning into beasts of the same burrow after death. How barbarous! Naturally that will not do today, because a husband remains, to the end, a husband, and a wife, whatever one says, remains a wife. The modern wife has trained up her sturdy individuality at a girls’ school in her divided skirt, and comes into marriage wearing her hair in Western style, so of course she cannot possibly act just as her husband wishes. For a wife who does everything as her husband wishes is no wife at all; she is a doll. The better the wife, the more fiercely her individuality develops, and the more it develops, the harder it becomes for her to get along with her husband. If they cannot get along, then naturally she comes into conflict with her husband. Therefore, so long as she bears the name of a good wife, she is in conflict with her husband from morning till night. This is, of course, splendid: the more one takes a good wife into one’s home, the more the suffering on both sides increases. Like water and oil, there is a sharp boundary between husband and wife, and if that boundary were calm and kept its balance, that would still be tolerable; but since water and oil both work upon each other from opposite sides, the household heaves up and down without end like a great earthquake. Thus humankind gradually comes to understand that mixed habitation by husband and wife is harmful to both parties...

paragraphs.source_en: Meitei continued, “It is our good fortune to have been born in the sacred reign of Meiji. As for me, precisely because I am capable of composing a Chronicle of the Future, my brain is one or two steps ahead of the times, and I have been living the single life since now. People chatter nonsense and insist it is the result of a failed romance; what these shortsighted folk can see is pitifully shallow. Leaving that aside, let me go on with my Chronicle of the Future. It runs like this: at that time, a philosopher will descend from heaven and advocate an unprecedented truth. His doctrine will say: Man is an animal of individuality. To destroy individuality brings about the same result as destroying humanity. If the meaning of humanity is to be fulfilled, this individuality must be preserved at any cost and, at the same time, developed. To be bound by vulgar custom and grudgingly carry out marriage is a corrupt practice contrary to the natural tendency of humanity; in an ignorant age when individuality was undeveloped, that might be another matter, but in civilized times like the present, to fall still into this evil and feel no surprise is an enormous error. In this present age, when the tide of enlightenment has reached its peak, there can be no reason why two individualities should be joined in a degree of intimacy beyond the ordinary. Despite this reason being as plain as daylight, uneducated young men and women, driven by a momentary base passion, carelessly perform the wedding rite; this is conduct of the most immoral and inhuman kind. For the sake of humanity, for the sake of civilization, and for the protection of those young men and women, we must resist this corrupt custom with all our strength...”
